A_general.open_code_note: No official public repository or package was found in the prepared repository list or official documentation. The endpoint is a hosted Workable server; its implementation could not be compared with public code.
A_general.release_status: Production-ready integration according to Workable; no separate MCP release-status label found.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Workable says MCP is available to customers on all plans at no added cost. Advanced Candidate Search and Advanced Employee Search require Premier+ or Enterprise. A Workable account and authorized user are required.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The pricing page lists Standard at $299/month or $3,588/year, Premier at $599/month or $7,188/year, and Enterprise at $719/month or $8,628/year for the displayed 1–20 employee band. Pricing varies by company size and billing option.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: MCP itself has no additional charge according to Workable. Plan and product availability still apply; advanced candidate and employee searches are limited to Premier+ and Enterprise. The pricing page also lists optional add-ons and AI credit packages, but does not state that MCP calls consume credits.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: OAuth sign-in is required. Calls use the signed-in user's Workable permissions and require an account subdomain on every tool except get_accounts. Relevant Workable products must be enabled; advanced searches are plan-restricted. Workable's MCP OAuth uses a pre-approved redirect-URI list. Calls are subject to Workable API rate limits.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Workable controls OAuth and plan/product availability; the Workable account administrator controls user roles and permissions; the authenticated user selects the account subdomain.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The official reference lists 94 tools covering recruiting, HR, account administration, time tracking and performance reviews. Workable documents Streamable HTTP, stateless JSON mode, without SSE or streaming. Read-only and write/destructive annotations are reported by Microsoft’s connector documentation.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The reference describes tool outputs in prose but does not reproduce complete tools/list schemas or a standard result envelope. Microsoft documents tool errors for unauthorized, forbidden, not found, conflict, unprocessable and rate-limited responses.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth 2.0 authorization code and refresh token grants; dynamic client registration; PKCE S256. Endpoint WWW-Authenticate advertises scope="r_candidates w_candidates r_jobs w_jobs r_offers w_offers r_requisitions w_requisitions w_comments r_account w_departments w_members r_employees w_employees r_timeoff w_timeoff r_time_tracking w_time_tracking r_reviews w_reviews r_reports r_surveys w_surveys". Protected-resource and authorization-server documents list scopes_supported: r_candidates, w_candidates, r_jobs, w_jobs, r_offers, w_offers, r_requisitions, w_requisitions, w_comments, r_account, w_departments, w_members, r_employees, w_employees, r_timeoff, w_timeoff, r_time_tracking, w_time_tracking, r_reviews, w_reviews, r_reports, r_surveys, w_surveys. Authorization endpoint https://workable.com/oauth/authorize; token endpoint https://workable.com/oauth/token; registration endpoint https://mcp.workable.com/oauth/register. Token lifetime, token authentication methods and revocation endpoint were not published in the supplied metadata. The help article says users can revoke authorization in Workable Settings > Integrations.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official list includes read and write operations. Microsoft describes read-only and destructive annotations; no official annotation payload or complete per-tool annotation table was found. 2. No mandatory confirm=true parameter or MCP elicitation documented. Several tool descriptions advise confirmation before final review actions; this is agent guidance. 3. OAuth scopes are broad and include read/write pairs for candidates, jobs, offers, requisitions, employees, time off, time tracking, reviews and surveys. Workable says authorization inherits the signed-in user's permissions. Microsoft reports a pre-approved redirect URI list and revocation via Settings > Integrations. Token lifetime is Unknown. 4. No read-only endpoint, toolset URL filter or query-free mode found. Server is stateless; account is selected explicitly. Advanced candidate/employee searches require Premier+ and Enterprise; HR tools depend on products enabled on the account. 5. No general PII masking policy found. Employee document access is said to respect Workable access permissions; detailed review answers are scoped to the caller. Candidate files may include temporary pre-signed preview URLs. 6. Calls are subject to Workable API rate limits; Microsoft says 429 errors ask the agent to retry after a short wait. Bulk time-entry tool allows up to 500 entries; review answer pagination limit is 1–200, default 50. No general MCP result truncation or call cost found. 7. Search tools expose field schemas and valid filter options; tool docs say invalid values can lead to 422 errors. Candidate tags/skills and review forms are replacement semantics. No operator defaults overriding model arguments documented. 8. MCP request logging, telemetry and opt-out are Unknown. Existing candidate/job activity log tools are available. 9. No vendor-feedback/rating tool identified in the official 94 names/descriptions. The OAuth scopes include r_surveys and w_surveys, but no survey-named tool appears in the official list. No MCP upsell response found. 10. No initialize instructions or server-delivered skills found. Tool descriptions include behavioral guidance; separate external skills were not located in the prepared evidence. 11. Server is stateless and does not push notifications; no documented persistent agent memory. 12. One hosted MCP endpoint with a flat tool list; account subdomains are tool arguments, not subservers. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution or general request escape hatch identified.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool reference lists 94 tools across its categories; the same total is stated in Workable's August 2026 article. actions.json contains all 94 official names. No catalogue-only tools were added: Claude's connector page exposes 24 visible names, all present in the official list, while its button states 45 tools total; the remaining names are not exposed in the captured page. Microsoft Learn describes the connector as having “just over 100 tools” and says deployment/account configuration can disable tools, so this count differs from Workable's published 94-tool list. The Microsoft page provides representative tools rather than a complete native-name list. Composio's separate Workable toolkit lists 37 proxy/API actions and was not treated as the input MCP server's tools.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code or verbatim initialize/tools/list payload was available; official reference descriptions are not complete schemas.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The MCP list does not expose tools for webhook subscription management or every operation in Workable's developer API. The API reference separately documents webhook subscription endpoints and broader Recruiting/HR operations; specific operations absent from the MCP list include creating webhook subscriptions and managing assessment/video-interview/background-check integrations. This compares exposed MCP tools with Workable's API documentation, not with every UI workflow.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Tool descriptions direct the agent to call get_accounts first and pass the chosen account on later calls; they also advise fetching and merging existing tags before replacement. Workable's help article says, “Always review what your AI assistant is about to do before confirming actions that modify data.” These are client/agent instructions; no universal server-enforced confirmation flow is documented.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Workable says MCP access is limited to the signed-in user's existing permissions. The help article says credentials are not stored by the AI client. Microsoft's connector page says the server “does not retain content beyond what is needed to serve the request”; this is third-party connector documentation, not a Workable MCP-specific retention clause. Workable's terms say AI-powered features are intended to support human decision-making and customers remain responsible for employment decisions; the terms do not clearly establish that this clause specifically governs external MCP clients.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Workable describes the MCP server as production-ready and available to all customers on all plans at no additional cost, with advanced candidate and employee searches limited to Premier+ and Enterprise. It says the authenticated user's permissions govern access and actions.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission inheritance is described both by Workable and the connector documentation, but implementation cannot be inspected because no public server code was found. The cited retention statement is from Microsoft connector documentation, and MCP-specific retention/logging controls were not independently documented by Workable. Confirmation-before-write language is guidance to review/confirm; no mandatory server-side confirmation mechanism was found.

contradictions: Workable's official reference and August 2026 article list 94 tools, while Microsoft's connector page says “just over 100 tools”; Microsoft also says the available list can vary by account or deployment, so the count may describe a different deployment state.

Claude's connector directory states “Show all 45 tools” but the captured page exposes only 24 names. All 24 visible names also occur in Workable's official list; the other 21 names could not be checked.

OAuth metadata advertises w_jobs, r_reports, r_surveys and w_surveys scopes, but the official 94-tool list has no job-write tools, report-specific tools or survey-specific tools. The metadata scopes therefore advertise access categories broader than the named MCP tool set.
observations_for_research: The server requires explicit account selection on every call except get_accounts, reducing ambiguity for users with multiple Workable accounts.

Several tool descriptions document irreversible or replacement-style effects and prompt the agent to confirm with the user, while separate annotations may allow a supporting client to request confirmation.
Advanced search is structured as field discovery, enum-option lookup and search, making valid filter choices discoverable at runtime.
The official tool reference provides names and descriptions but not complete MCP input schemas, limiting independent assessment of required parameters and validation.
